c1-1c-001.gate_key: narrative_b2 | B2.2 | gap | What are you doing with that tape measure? I ___ the kitchen for the new cupboards. (measure) |

item.q: What are you doing with that tape measure? I ___ the kitchen for the new cupboards. (measure)
item.why: *measure* here is an action happening now (using a tape measure): present continuous, *I'm measuring*.
item.why_lv: *measure te* ir darbība, kas notiek tagad (mēra ar mērlenti): Present Continuous, *I'm measuring.*

c1-1c-002.gate_key: narrative_b2 | B2.2 | gap | Our kitchen is tiny: it ___ only three metres by four. (measure) |

item.q: Our kitchen is tiny: it ___ only three metres by four. (measure)
item.why: *measure* here gives the size, a state: present simple, *it measures*. The continuous is used only for the action of measuring.
item.why_lv: *measure te* norāda izmēru, tas ir stāvoklis: Present Simple, *it measures*. Ilgstošo formu lieto *tikai* darbībai (kāds mēra).

c1-1c-003.gate_key: narrative_b2 | B2.2 | gap | My manager ___ taking early retirement, but she hasn't made up her mind yet. (consider) |

item.q: My manager ___ taking early retirement, but she hasn't made up her mind yet. (consider)
item.why: *consider* in the meaning *think carefully about* is only used in the continuous: *she's considering taking early retirement*.
item.why_lv: *consider* nozīmē rūpīgi apsvērt lieto *tikai* ilgstošajā formā: *she's considering taking early retirement*.

c1-1c-004.gate_key: narrative_b2 | B2.2 | text | Your friend changes the order for the third time: "Actually, I'll have the fish, not the pasta." Complain, using *constantly* and *change your mind*. |

accepted: You are constantly changing your mind.

item.q: Your friend changes the order for the third time: "Actually, I'll have the fish, not the pasta." Complain, using *constantly* and *change your mind*.
item.why: *be constantly* + *-ing* shows that something happens so often that it is typical of the person, often with irritation: *You're constantly changing your mind.*
item.why_lv: *be constantly + -ing* rāda, ka kaut kas notiek tik bieži, ka tas ir raksturīgi cilvēkam, bieži ar *nepatiku*: *You're constantly changing your mind.*
answers: You are constantly changing your mind.

c1-1c-005.gate_key: narrative_b2 | B2.2 | gap | Write one word in each gap: Don't phone me at half past eight: I ___ usually ___ to work then. (drive) |

item.q: Write one word in each gap: Don't phone me at half past eight: I ___ usually ___ to work then. (drive)
item.why: *usually* + present continuous: something we regularly do that is in progress at that time (*I'm usually driving to work then*).
item.why_lv: *usually* + Present Continuous: *ierasta* darbība, kas tajā laikā jau notiek (*I'm usually driving to work then*).

c1-1c-006.gate_key: narrative_b2 | B2.2 | mcq | Which sentence has a mistake? | My neighbour forever is borrowing my tools.

key.correct: My neighbour forever is borrowing my tools.
wrong: He's always offering to help with the shopping.
At eight I'm usually driving to work.
She constantly checks her phone in meetings.

item.why: *forever*, *always*, *constantly* go after *is*: *My neighbour is forever borrowing my tools.*
item.why_lv: *forever, always, constantly* stāv aiz *is*: *My neighbour is forever borrowing my tools.*
item.correct: My neighbour forever is borrowing my tools.
wrong: He's always offering to help with the shopping.
At eight I'm usually driving to work.
She constantly checks her phone in meetings.

c1-1c-007.gate_key: narrative_b2 | B2.2 | order | Put the words in order. | you're constantly interrupting me when I'm speaking

key.sentence: you're constantly interrupting me when I'm speaking
also: when I'm speaking you're constantly interrupting me
you're interrupting me constantly when I'm speaking
when I'm speaking you're interrupting me constantly

item.why: *constantly* goes between *you're* and the *-ing* form; the *when*-part can come first or second.
item.why_lv: *constantly* stāv starp *you're* un *-ing* formu; daļa ar *when* var būt pirmā vai otrā.
item.sentence: you're constantly interrupting me when I'm speaking
answers: you're constantly interrupting me when I'm speaking
when I'm speaking you're constantly interrupting me
you're interrupting me constantly when I'm speaking

c1-1c-008.gate_key: narrative_b2 | B2.2 | mcq | Which sentence has a mistake? | This suitcase is weighing 23 kilos, so it's just under the limit.

key.correct: This suitcase is weighing 23 kilos, so it's just under the limit.
wrong: The vet is weighing the dog right now.
This scarf feels lovely and soft.
They're fitting a new kitchen in our flat this week.

item.why: *weigh* for the weight of something is a state: *This suitcase weighs 23 kilos*. *The vet is weighing the dog* is the action, so the continuous is right there.
item.why_lv: *weigh svara* nozīmē ir stāvoklis: *This suitcase weighs 23 kilos.* *The vet is weighing the dog* ir darbība, tāpēc tur Continuous forma ir *pareiza*.
item.correct: This suitcase is weighing 23 kilos, so it's just under the limit.
wrong: The vet is weighing the dog right now.
This scarf feels lovely and soft.
They're fitting a new kitchen in our flat this week.

c1-1c-009.gate_key: narrative_b2 | B2.2 | gap | Write to a customer: We ___ for the delay in replying to your email. (apologise) |

item.q: Write to a customer: We ___ for the delay in replying to your email. (apologise)
item.why: When the words themselves are the act (apologising by saying it), use the present simple: *We apologise for the delay*, not *We're apologising*.
item.why_lv: Ja paši vārdi ir darbība (*atvainojamies, to sakot*), lieto Present Simple: *We apologise for the delay*, nevis *We're apologising.*

c1-1c-010.gate_key: narrative_b2 | B2.2 | mcq | Which is the usual way to write this as a news headline? | Health minister resigns over expenses

wrong: Health minister has resigned over expenses
Health minister is resigning over expenses

item.q: Which is the usual way to write this as a news headline?
item.why: Headlines use the present simple for an event that has just happened: *Health minister resigns*. In a normal sentence we would say *has resigned*.
item.why_lv: *Virsrakstos* par *tikko* notikušu *lietu* lieto Present Simple: *Health minister resigns.* Parastā teikumā *teiktu has resigned*.
wrong: Health minister has resigned over expenses
Health minister is resigning over expenses
